title: Build kit manifest
description: Describes a stack for a builder host: how a project is scaffolded, what the agent is told, how a slice is built and verified, and how the work lands in Git. Written as build-kit.yaml or build-kit.json at the root of the kit. Version 1.

kitVersion.description: The version of this manifest format.

name.description: The kit's name, lowercase words joined by hyphens. Registered kits are installed by it.

version.description: The kit's own version, as semantic version.

description.description: One sentence on the stack the kit builds.

versions.description: The build order and outcome contract versions the kit's prompt is written for. Defaults to ["1"].

schemaVersions.description: The compiled Screenplay model schema versions the kit understands, such as ">=38" or ">=38 <50".

sliceTypes.description: The slice types the kit builds. A builder host takes no order for another type.

ui.description: Whether the kit also builds user interfaces (the ui part of an order).

scaffold.description: How a new project is created: a folder of files copied into an empty project, commands run in it, or both.

instructions.description: The stack instructions, a Markdown file. Installed in the form the chosen agent reads.

skills.description: A folder of skills, one folder per skill holding a SKILL.md.

prompt.description: The prompt template for one build order. Placeholders in braces are filled from the order.

verify.description: Commands the host runs after the agent is done, in order. A slice is reported built only when every one exits with 0.

branch.description: The branch to build on, such as "studio/{feature}".

permissions.description: What the host allows when the agent asks for permission. Everything else is refused.

paths.description: Globs, relative to the project, the agent may write. Defaults to everything in the project.

commands.description: Command prefixes the agent may run, such as "dotnet build". The verify commands are always allowed.

existingCodebase.description: How the kit builds into a project it did not scaffold: the agent learns the project's conventions once, records them, and every later build reads them.

learn.description: The prompt that asks the agent to learn the project's conventions.

conventions.description: Where in the project the learned conventions are recorded, such as ".cratis/build/conventions.md".

requires.description: Tools the host checks for before it builds.

path.description: A path inside the kit, starting with ./ and never leaving it.

projectPath.description: A path inside the project, relative, never leaving it.
